conclusion: Supreme court disposition (Standard rent appeal): The Supreme Court allowed Civil Appeal 464 of 1971 and remitted to the District Judge the landlord appeal concerning the standard-rent determination. Supreme court disposition (Eviction and interim rent proceedings): The Supreme Court allowed Civil Appeals 465-466 of 1971, remitted to the trial court for proceedings on merits, and restored the tenant ability to defend; interim rent remained to be determined. Supreme court recounted fact (limitation of standard-rent application): The premises were let directly by the landlord to the particular applicant tenant with the relevant tenancy commencing after the commencement of the Act. Supreme court recounted procedural fact (limitation of standard-rent application): The applicant filed the Section 8 petition within six months from commencement of that applicant's relevant tenancy. Supreme court recounted fact (classification of tenancy and interpretation of limitation): The head tenant inducted the appellant as subtenant after the Act commenced. Supreme court evidentiary assessment (classification of tenancy and interpretation of limitation): The record contains no evidence showing that the landlord gave written consent to the appellant's induction as subtenant. Admitted position recognized by supreme court (classification of tenancy and interpretation of limitation): After Brook surrendered the head tenancy, the landlord expressly accepted the appellant as direct tenant from May 1, 1955. Reported lower court reasoning (rejected lower-court construction): The District Judge adopted the earlier subtenancy or first letting as the starting point for calculating the appellant's limitation period, and the High Court substantially endorsed that reasoning. Reported lower court reasoning (rejected lower-court construction): The September 1, 1954 induction as Brook's subtenant is legally the controlling letting for the appellant's Section 11(b) application after direct tenancy was recognized from May 1, 1955. Landlord claim reported (eviction protection and possession proceedings): The landlord brought a possession suit asserting failure to pay rent after the statutory demand notice under Section 13(1)(a). Supreme court recounted fact (eviction protection and possession proceedings): During the eviction proceedings, the tenant deposited the arrears claimed by the landlord. Supreme court recounted procedural fact (interim management of contested rent in eviction litigation): A tenant's application for determination of standard rent was pending while the landlord pursued eviction for nonpayment. Supreme court recounted procedural fact (interim management of contested rent in eviction litigation): The tenant applied under Section 9 for interim-rent determination while the standard-rent question remained pending. Supreme court legal and evidentiary finding (validity of rent-deposit direction and procedural sanction): No legally operative interim-rent determination resolving the tenant's Section 9 application had been made.
